name: Meal Planner
description: The family's meals for every day of the week, a running-out guess for the things they buy from their order history, and a reminder each afternoon and evening with one cart per shopping app that is ordered only when they say yes; not for school runs, chores or appointments.

for: The family's meals for the week, planned every Sunday for every day of the week, each with its dishes
A guess of what is running out (atta, dal, oil) from the family's own order history on their shopping apps
A reminder at 3 pm and 7 pm with tonight's or tomorrow's meals, the items that may be running low and one cart per shopping app, ordered only when the family says yes
The family's saved recipes and each dish's video, planned into the week, and how each dish went last time
notFor: School runs, chores or appointments (use checklist or tracker)
Keeping a list of what is in the kitchen: it only guesses what is running out
A restaurant's menu or a business kitchen

setupMenu: Planning the week's meals and groceries

setupOptions.about: Learn how this family eats and shops. Never brands, pack sizes or what's at home, or whether to add a regular. Nothing is ordered now. Each reply is read only into its facts; at the end the Meal Planner saves the whole setup itself from the household facts and the replies word for word (apply_setup), and its read-back is checked with the family.

routines.name: Weekly meal plan
routines.description: Every Sunday at 11, plans next week's meals, every day of it, in steps (the menu checked against every food rule, then each day's ingredients), saves the week, and asks the agent only to send the family the plan. It plans only: nothing is bought. On an install carried over from the old Meal Planner it first asks for the family's profile to be structured.

routines.name: Afternoon reminder
routines.description: Every day at 3 pm, when there is something to say: tonight's dinner, the ingredients to check, what you buy every day put on the cart as it comes due, and anything that may be running low. Nothing is ordered until you reply.

routines.name: Evening reminder
routines.description: Every day at 7 pm: reads new orders from your connected shopping apps, then tells you tomorrow's meals, puts what you buy every day on the cart as it comes due and asks about anything that may be running low. Nothing is ordered until you reply.

routines.name: Order clock
routines.description: Every 15 minutes: an order not paid within 24 hours is closed and its items go back on your cart (you are told once); an order stuck being placed for an hour goes back to your cart.

intents.name: sync-cart
intents.description: The family changed or opened their cart in Meal Planner: make the app's own cart match it.
intents.instructions: The payload has order_id, app and lines [{ item, product_id, name_on_app, qty }]. With that app's connector, make its cart hold exactly these lines (qty 0: take it off); touch only lines Meal Planner put there, and list any other line already in the cart as outside_lines. Read the cart back and call sync_cart { order_id, lines, total, delivery_gap, outside_lines }. A line the app does not have today (in_stock false): when the family has a fallback app (shopping.fallback in GET /api/family), take it off with set_cart_line { item, qty: 0, app } and move it with set_cart_line { item, qty, app: <fallback> }, then copy that cart to the fallback app and sync_cart it too; with no fallback, leave it marked. Send no message.

operations.name: guide
operations.description: The full guide for working with this app: read it before the first conversation, or when you are not sure which operation fits. {}

operations.name: set_person
operations.description: Add or change one person who eats at home, found by name. { name, relationship?, group?: child | adult | elder, portions?, diet?, allergies?, dislikes?, targets?, note?, remove?: true }. group is needed for a new person. Keep portions, diet and the rest in the family's own words. Only the fields you send change; null clears one; remove: true takes the person out of the family.

operations.name: set_house_rules
operations.description: The house's food rules. { rules?: [{ kind, who?, days?, slots?, items?, to?, per_week?, per_meal?, note? }], add?: true, notes?, structured?: true }. Send at least one of rules, notes and structured. The rules you send replace the ones there, so send the whole list; with add: true they are added to the ones there instead (a rule already there is not added twice). Answers { house, said: every rule in plain words, a line for everyone and one per person }. The app checks every plan against the checked kinds and refuses one that breaks them (RULE_BROKEN, naming each break): avoid { items, who?, days?, slots? } no dish who eats has any of items; only { who, items, slots?, days? } every dish who eats there is one of items (dish names: "plain idli"); a fast is only with its days (Nani on Thu: sabudana khichdi, fruit); swap { who, items, to } a dish who eats with any of items carries a portion_note naming who and to ("millet idli for Nani"), or who gets a dish of their own; require { slots, items, who? } in each of slots who (everyone when left out) eats a dish with one of items; cap { items, per_week } dishes with items in at most per_week meals a week; or cap { per_meal, slots?, days?, items?, who? } at most per_meal dishes to cook in each meal of slots (dishes with items when given; sides such as chutney, podi, curd, fruit, pickle not counted; a variant for one person is a dish of its own, so serve one dish to more people, or a swap as a portion_note). A cap takes per_week or per_meal, not both. who is one person's name as on the Family page (set_person first); days are weekdays (Mon..Sun), left out for every day; slots are meal names (Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner or an extra slot), left out for every meal. items are words matched in a dish's name and ingredients, or categories: @meat, @fish, @egg, @nuts, @peanut, @root_veg, @green_leafy, @white_rice (millet, brown, red and ragi rice are not), @protein, @vegan_protein, @dal, @dairy, @soy, @gluten, @sweet (a dish named "no sugar" is not sweet by its name), @chilli, @pickle, @mushroom, @baked. note keeps the family's own words. The older kinds still work: veg, no_meat and egg (eggs but no meat) avoid meat and fish; no_eggs avoids eggs; no_onion_garlic avoids onion and garlic; fasting { who, days, slots, note } is checked: no dish for who at those slots on those days ("fasts Monday till evening": slots Breakfast, Lunch); a fasting rule without slots, and other, are notes only (other says the rule in its note; their days may be the family's own word for a day, "Ekadashi"). A cook's limit is a rule with no who: specific dishes avoid { items: ["chole"] }, no oven avoid { items: ["@baked"] }, "phulkas twice a week" cap { items: ["phulka"], per_week: 2 }; read back to the family from said. The grocery app is not set here: use set_shopping_apps. notes is free text, or a list of lines. Send structured: true once a profile carried over from the old app is fully in people, rules, the cook and slots, and at least one person is saved: it clears that text.

operations.name: set_cook
operations.description: The cook: who, which days, when they arrive, what they make well, what they do not make well or will not make, their time, and whether they try new recipes. { name, days?: ["Mon", ...], arrival?: "HH:MM" (a cook who comes more than once a day: a list of visits, ["06:00", "16:30"] or [{ at: "06:00", meals: ["Breakfast", "Lunch"] }, { at: "16:30", meals: ["Dinner"] }]; meals are slot names), makes_well?, wont_make?, time_limit?: in the family's words ("off to the next house at 9: a dish or two in the morning"), new_recipes?: open (tries recipes from reels and the internet) | set_menu (better with familiar dishes), note? }. name every time; days and arrival the first time. Only what you send changes; null clears a field. Plans never give the cook what is in wont_make, fit time_limit, and keep to familiar dishes with set_menu. A cook's limit said any time (in chat, or fixing a plan: "swap the chole, the cook can't make it") is saved at once as a checked house rule, with set_house_rules { add: true }, and its words in wont_make: dishes named: {"kind":"avoid","items":["chole"],"note":"the cook can't make it"}; "no baking, no oven": {"kind":"avoid","items":["@baked"],"note":"no oven"}; "phulkas only twice a week": {"kind":"cap","items":["phulka"],"per_week":2}. A vague limit ("no fancy stuff") stays words only; ask "which dishes?" once when it matters. A plan correction saves the limit too, not only the swap.

operations.name: set_slots
operations.description: Meals beyond Breakfast, Lunch and Dinner, and the meals the family orders in or eats out every week (not cooked at home; every other meal of every day is planned). { extra_slots?: [{ name, days?: ["Mon", ...], for?: [names] }], order_in?: [{ day: "Sun", slot: "Dinner", note? }], add?: true }. A child's school tiffin is an extra slot: { name: "Kabir's tiffin", days: ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri"], for: ["Kabir"] }, an evening snack { name: "Evening snack" } (no for: everyone's, unless the family names who); a plan gives each a meal on each of its days. Send at least one of the two lists. With add: true (always, when the family tells you of a meal) they are added to the ones there: a slot of the same name, or an order_in of the same day and slot, takes that one's place, and nothing said before is lost. Without add each list sent replaces the one there (only to take a slot out: the whole list without it). An order_in slot is Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner or an extra slot's name. Answers { house, said: the meals each week is planned with, in plain words }.

operations.name: set_cooking_days
operations.description: Only for a day nothing at all is cooked at home: every day is planned, and a day the cook does not come is cooked by the family. { days: ["mon", "tue", ...] }: the days food is cooked at home, at least one, any capitals; the cook's days always stay. Each meal of a day left out is saved as not cooked at home (as set_slots order_in), and a day named again is cooked again. One meal out is set_slots { add: true, order_in }. Answers { house, slots_said }.

operations.name: set_shopping_apps
operations.description: The family's shopping apps. { main: zepto | swiggy-instamart | zomato-blinkit | bigbasket | amazon, fallback: the app to try when something is not on the main one, or null, connected: [only the apps the family has signed in to in Flock; [] when none yet] }. Apps by id or name ("Blinkit"). main and fallback may be apps not signed in to yet, and are never added to connected: send the call again after each sign-in. Order history is read, and a cart copied, only for a connected app; fallback must differ from main. Answers { main, fallback, connected, order_without_asking, house }.

operations.name: apply_setup
operations.description: Save the family's whole meal setup at the end of the interview, in one call. { household: every household fact you hold (people, help at home, routines), transcript: the planner's questions and the family's replies, word for word and in order, as lines "Q: ..." and "A: ..." (corrections, later and off-topic replies included, as they happened) }. The app reads them itself and saves the people, the cook (every day is planned: the cook's days off, the family cooks), the extra meals (one said without names is everyone's) and the meals eaten out or ordered in, the food rules (only what the family said), the family's dishes, the shopping apps and subscriptions. Answers { ok, said: what was saved in plain words, to read back to the family (send it word for word, then ask if anything should change; a correction is the same call again with the reply added to the transcript), noted: what was kept but is not checked, dropped } or { ok: false, say }.

operations.name: plan_week
operations.description: Plan a week of meals. { week_start: the week's Monday as YYYY-MM-DD, mode: draft | final, keep_rest?: true, meals?: [{ date, slot, ordered_in?: true, note?, dishes?: [{ name, for: ["everyone"] or [names], except?: [names] (with everyone: everyone but them), portion_note?, recipe_id?, video_url?, ingredients: [{ item, amount?, unit? }] }] }] }. Without meals it answers with the context to plan from (people, house, bought_often: what the house buys often, last week's dishes, known_dishes: how each dish went last time and its video, the recipe book; plan a dish rated didnt_work rarely and heed every note), or, when mode is final and the week is a draft, makes that draft final. With meals they become the whole week's plan, in place of what was there; with keep_rest: true only the meals at the dates and slots you send are replaced and the rest of the week stays. A call carries 16 KB at most, so send a week one day a call: each day with mode final and keep_rest: true, then one closing call with mode final and no meals. Send meals with mode draft only when the family asks you to propose a week. A meal is planned once, not once per person: a slot has one dish for everyone who eats it, and one person's variation is that dish's portion_note ("two eggs for Arjun", "no eggs on Tuesday"), never a second dish. Every dish names who eats it in for: ["everyone"] (everyone who eats that meal; a tiffin's own people) or the names on the Family page; a dish without is refused (MISSING_EATERS, naming each dish). Plan a second dish only when someone truly eats something else (a baby's milk, an elder's softer dish, Kabir's plain idli): it names only them, and the shared dish is for everyone except them (for: ["everyone"], except: [their names]). A swap stays a portion_note on a dish they eat ("millet instead of rice for Nani"). The same dish sent twice in a meal is kept as one, eaten by all of theirs. amount is a number above 0 with its measure in unit, for this family; an ordered-in meal has no dishes. Every day of the week is planned; a meal the family eats out or orders in is ordered_in: true. In a final call every dish needs its ingredients (refused with MISSING_INGREDIENTS, naming the dishes). Only the closing call, mode final without meals (it also works on a week already final), answers message, intro (the first time only) and instructions: forward message verbatim (its links are the only ones to send), then intro once, then end your turn; final calls with meals answer none of them. The closing call is refused, naming what to fix, while a dish has no ingredients, an extra slot (a tiffin) has no meal on one of its days, or a main dish is on more than two days (REPEATED_DISHES; roti, rice, sides and a person's only dishes aside). set_meal and set_dish (the family's changes) never check repeats. Answers { week } or { context }, with message, intro and instructions on the closing call. A final plan (or a change to one) that breaks a food rule on the Family page is refused with RULE_BROKEN, every break named in rule_breaks: fix each (a dish of their own for a person, a portion_note for a swap) and send again.

operations.name: make_plan
operations.description: Plan a whole week and save it final, in one call: { week_start: the week's Monday as YYYY-MM-DD }. The app plans it in steps itself (the menu from the family's own dishes, checked against every food rule, every meal and extra slot, and no main dish on more than two days; then each day's ingredients), the same way the Sunday run does, and messages nobody. Answers { ok: true, week_start, message, intro?, instructions, unmet? } (send message word for word, then intro once, as instructions say; unmet: what could not be kept, already said in message) or { ok: false, reason, say } (nothing planned: send say word for word). Use it when the family asks for a week planned or planned again; set_meal and set_dish change one meal.

operations.name: plan_menu
operations.description: The whole week's menu in one call, before any ingredients: { week_start: the week's Monday, meals: [{ date, slot, ordered_in?: true, note?, dishes?: [{ name, for: ["everyone"] or [names], except?: [names] (with everyone: everyone but them), portion_note? }] }] (every meal of every day of the week, its extra slots too) }. Every main dish is new to the week (on two days at most) and at most 3–4 come from last week's dishes; roti, rice, sides (chutney, curd, plain dal) and a person's only dishes come back as needed; what the family said wins. The app checks it as a whole: who eats each dish (MISSING_EATERS), the food rules a dish's name shows (RULE_BROKEN, every break named in rule_breaks), each extra slot's days (MISSING_SLOTS), and no main dish on more than two days (REPEATED_DISHES). Refused with every problem named: fix them all and send the whole menu again. Kept as the week's draft when it passes; then give each day its ingredients with plan_week (mode final, keep_rest: true, one day a call, the same dish names and for) and close with plan_week final. Answers { week, next }.

operations.name: set_meal
operations.description: Change one meal, found by date and slot (or meal_id) and made when it is not there. { date, slot, or meal_id; ordered_in?, note?, dishes?: [as in plan_week, each with for (who eats it: ["everyone"] or the names) and its ingredients] }. Only what you send changes; dishes you send replace the meal's dishes. ordered_in: true takes its dishes away; sending dishes with it is refused, and a meal that is ordered in takes dishes only with ordered_in: false. A meal keeps its date and slot. Answers { meal }. A final plan (or a change to one) that breaks a food rule on the Family page is refused with RULE_BROKEN, every break named in rule_breaks: fix each (a dish of their own for a person, a portion_note for a swap) and send again.

operations.name: set_dish
operations.description: Add, change or remove one dish. { dish_id, or meal_id, or date and slot; name?, for?: ["everyone"] or [names], except?: [names] (with everyone: everyone but them), portion_note?, recipe_id?, video_url?, ingredients?: [{ item, amount?, unit? }], position?, remove?: true }. A dish you add needs its ingredients, and keeps them: one left without is refused. A dish you add names who eats it in for: ["everyone"] (everyone who eats that meal) or names on the Family page (MISSING_EATERS without); a person's own dish names only them, and the shared dish is for everyone except them (for: ["everyone"], except: [their names]); a swap stays a portion_note on a dish they eat ("millet instead of rice for Nani"). Without dish_id, name is needed: in that meal a dish of the same name is the one changed; otherwise it is added at the end (and the meal made when it is not there). By dish_id a name you send renames it. Only what you send changes; ingredients you send replace the dish's; position 0 is first; a dish already there keeps its for unless you send one. Answers { dish, meal }; remove: true answers { meal }. A final plan (or a change to one) that breaks a food rule on the Family page is refused with RULE_BROKEN, every break named in rule_breaks: fix each (a dish of their own for a person, a portion_note for a swap) and send again.

operations.name: set_regular
operations.description: The older way to state an item's cycle, kept so earlier instructions still work; set_item is the one to use. { item, amount, unit, every: day | week | weekdays, times_per_week?, weekdays?: ["Mon", ...], for_whom?, active?, paused_until?: YYYY-MM-DD, remove?: true }. The same as set_item { item, usual_amount, unit, every_days }: amount with unit is what is bought each time; every with times_per_week or weekdays is how often (1 l every day; every: week with times_per_week: 2 is twice a week). It is kept on the item as its cycle and shown on the Pantry page; there is no separate list. paused_until snoozes the item up to and including that date; active: false or remove: true takes the stated cycle away; for_whom is not kept (an item has one cycle for the house). Answers { item }.

operations.name: import_order_history
operations.description: Give the app the family's past orders on one shopping app, one app a call; read them with that app's connector first (Amazon's cannot be read). { app: zepto | swiggy-instamart | zomato-blinkit | bigbasket | amazon (by id or name), account?: which of your accounts of this app, when you hold more than one (its account id, else its label; always the same one), orders: [{ date: YYYY-MM-DD, order_ref?: the app's order id, items: [{ item, group: daily | few_days | monthly (as set_item names them; send it with every item, so none is left to set one by one), product?, product_id?, pack?: "5 kg", pack_amount?, pack_unit?, count?, price?, image?: the product's picture link from the order's details }] }] }. item is the family's word for it (atta), product the name on the app, image the product's picture as the app's order details give it (Zepto's order detail, Instamart's order items), never one you made or searched for; count is how many packs (1 when left out). Send the oldest orders first, at most about 8 orders and 80 items a call, one app a call (a call carries 16 KB at most), and only the last 3 months: older orders are skipped, and so is an order dated after today. Send only delivered or paid orders, never a cancelled or failed one. Each item becomes a purchase; the same order sent again is recorded once, so a call may overlap the last. An item with its product_id is remembered as that app's product. More than one person may order for the house, each on their own account of the same app: each person's agent gives the orders of that person's account, and all of them count towards one cycle per item for the house. Holding more than one account of an app (Zepto (Arjun), Zepto (Meera)), read each and send each with its account: each has its own read_until, and an order with no order_ref is never taken for one of another account. The app works out each item's cycle (how much, how often) from the purchases by itself: ask the family to confirm nothing. Answers { recorded, duplicates, skipped_old, skipped_future, needs_group: [items to give a group with set_item], probably_out: [{ item, days_ago }], read_until: how far you have read this app, or this account of it (YYYY-MM-DD), said: what the house buys most often and how often, in a line ("milk (1 l every day), eggs (30 pc once a week)"), "" when nothing yet }.

operations.name: record_bought_outside
operations.description: The family bought an item outside the apps ("got atta from the kirana"). { item, date?: YYYY-MM-DD, today when left out }. It counts as a purchase of the usual amount and restarts the item's estimate. Answers { event_id } or { duplicate: true }, and { item }.

operations.name: set_item
operations.description: Change one item the family buys, made when it is not there. { item, group?: daily | few_days | monthly (how often it is bought: daily every day or two, like milk; few_days within the week, like vegetables, eggs, bread; monthly lasts weeks, like atta, oil, masalas, cleaning and personal care), usual_amount?: what is bought each time, a number in unit, unit?: g | kg | ml | l | pc, every_days?: how many days one purchase lasts (1: every day; 7: once a week), follows_plan?: true when the week's meals use it up (paneer, rajma), dont_ask?: true to never ask about it or put it on the cart by itself, snooze_days?: days to leave it alone, for a holiday (null clears) }. usual_amount and every_days are the item's cycle as the family said it ("milk every day, 1 litre": { item: "milk", group: "daily", usual_amount: 1, unit: "l", every_days: 1 }; "a tray of 30 eggs once a week": usual_amount: 30, unit: "pc", every_days: 7): send them only when the family says so or there is no order history, since the app works the cycle out from the purchases and goes by those once they show one; null clears either. A daily item with a cycle goes on the cart by itself when it is due; the others are asked about. Only what you send changes. Answers { item }.

operations.name: set_subscription
operations.description: An item delivered outside the apps (Country Delight, a milkman). { item, source: who delivers it, active: true | false }. active: true keeps it out of every cart and every question about running low, and takes it off the carts not yet ordered; active: false makes it an item like any other again. Answers { item }.

operations.name: answer_running_low
operations.description: The family's answers to "still in stock?". { answers: [{ item, answer: low | in_stock, days?: how many more days it will last }] }. low: it goes on the cart (answers { to_cart }). in_stock with days ("fine for a week": 7) is not asked again until then; in_stock without days ("still have it") waits a few days. Answers { to_cart: [items to add to the cart], items }.

operations.name: get_reminder
operations.description: The reminder to send now, built from the plan, the carts and what may be running low. { which: afternoon | evening, date?: the date the reminder's wake gave, YYYY-MM-DD (so a call after midnight builds that same reminder) }. afternoon is tonight's dinner, evening is tomorrow's meals; both put the daily items due tomorrow (by each item's cycle) on the cart and ask about at most 5 items that may be running low, each counted once per reminder however often you call it. Answers { which, date, meals, ask_ingredients, added, cart_items, asks: [{ item, days_ago }], delivery_gap, ordered: [{ order_id, app, message }], empty, text, app_text, block, carts: [{ order_id, app, status, lines, sync }] }. empty: send nothing. Send text on WhatsApp word for word, or app_text with block in the app chat. Read the connected apps' new orders into import_order_history before the first call. Copy each cart with sync: true to its app, then sync_cart, then call get_reminder again with the same which and date and send that answer. Check out every cart in ordered (Order without asking is on; a retry lists the same ones): say its message, check out, record_order.

operations.name: get_cart
operations.description: The carts: one open cart per shopping app, and any being ordered. { app?: one app by id or name }. Answers { carts: [{ order_id, app, app_name, status: open | ordering, lines: [{ id, item, qty, product_id, name_on_app, pack, price, source, for_note }], total, delivery_gap, sync_state, synced_at, outside_lines, building_at_order }] }. A line at qty 0 is shown, not ordered.

operations.name: set_cart_line
operations.description: Put an item on the cart, change its qty or take it off. { item, qty: packs, a whole number (0 takes it off), app?: the app (else the one the family buys it on, else the main app), source?: added (default) | low | everyday | meal, for_note?, for_date?: YYYY-MM-DD, product_id?, name_on_app?, pack?, price?, image?: the product's picture link as the app gives it }. It goes on that app's open cart; while a cart is being ordered, a new item goes to a new open cart, and you may lower or take off a line of the cart being ordered ("remove the ghee"), and a higher qty or a new item goes to the open cart. An item delivered outside the apps is refused (code SUBSCRIPTION). Copy the change to the app's own cart yourself in the same turn, then sync_cart. Answers { line, cart }.

operations.name: order_cart
operations.description: The family said yes to ordering one app's cart (a reply, or the message "Order my <App> cart" from the Order button). { app }. The cart is being ordered from now on, and anything added later goes to a new cart. Send its message word for word, check out on the app, then record_order. Asked again while that order is being placed, it answers the same order. Answers { order_id, app, lines, message }; an empty cart is refused (409).

operations.name: sync_cart
operations.description: What the app's own cart holds after you copied a cart to it, or read it back. { order_id, lines: [{ product_id, qty, price?, in_stock?: false when the app does not have it today }], total?: the app's cart total, delivery_gap?: rupees short of free delivery, outside_lines?: [{ name, qty? }] (lines in the app's cart Meal Planner did not put there) }. Answers { cart }.

operations.name: record_order
operations.description: What happened to an order being placed. { order_id, placed?: true, paid?: true | false, app_order_ref?: the app's order id, total? }. placed: its lines become purchases and the items' estimates restart. paid: false (not paid): the purchases stop counting and the lines go back on the open cart; paid: true later brings both back. When you record paid: false, tell the family yourself: the clock will not. Send app_order_ref whenever you have it, also later. Answers { order }, and taken_off: [{ order_id, items }] when a late payment took returned items off a cart being ordered: take them off that checkout on the app too.

operations.name: cancel_order
operations.description: Stop an order. { order_id }. One being ordered goes back to the open cart (nothing was placed); a placed one counts as not paid, its lines back on the cart, and you tell the family so yourself: the clock will not. Answers { order }.

operations.name: remember_product
operations.description: Remember the product an item is bought as on a grocery app, so the next order reuses it without searching. { item, app: zepto | swiggy-instamart | zomato-blinkit | bigbasket, product_id, name_on_app, pack?, pack_amount?, pack_unit?, price?, image? }. item is the family's word for it, exactly as on the order line or the pantry item (milk), never the product's name on the app; pack_amount and pack_unit are the pack's size as a number and its measure (500, ml), which the app counts packs with (a plain pack text like "500 ml" is read too). One product per item and app: sending it again takes the place of the one remembered. Answers { product }.

operations.name: save_recipe
operations.description: Save a recipe, or change one. { recipe_id?, name?, links?: [the reel, short or page], notes?, ingredients?: [{ item, amount?, unit? }], tags?: ["breakfast", "tiffin"], for?: [names], thumbnail? }. Without recipe_id, a recipe that already holds one of the links is the one changed (new links are added to it), so a link shared twice is saved once; otherwise a new recipe is made, and it needs a name: with none the answer is code NEEDS_NAME, so ask the family what to call it and save again. By recipe_id only what you send changes, and links you send replace its links. Answers { recipe }; put its id on a dish with set_dish recipe_id.

operations.name: set_family_dishes
operations.description: The family's own dishes, from what each person ate over the past week: { dishes: [{ name, slots: [the meals it is eaten at: Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner or an extra slot such as a tiffin], for?: [names on the Family page, only when one person eats it], often?: usually | sometimes | rarely, per_week?: days a week, days?: [weekdays], remove?: true }] }. How often only when the family said it. Each dish once, with every meal it is eaten at; sent again, it takes the meals and eaters sent. The weekly plan is built from these (the context's family_dishes). Answers { family_dishes } by meal.

operations.name: set_dish_video
operations.description: Give a dish its one video, or take it away. { dish: its name as planned, or dish_id, url: the link (a YouTube video, an Instagram reel, any page; never a file), title?, thumbnail?: the video's picture link, remove?: true }. The video is the dish's, kept by its name: every week the dish is planned it shows on the Week page and in the cook's message, with no call again. Find one with your own search when the family asks ("find a video for rajma"); a recipe or reel the family shares for a dish is its video too. A YouTube link's thumbnail is filled in when you send none. A second video takes the place of the first. Answers { dish: { name, video, rating, note, rated_on, said_by, history } }.

operations.name: rate_dishes
operations.description: How dishes went when the family ate them. { date?: the day they were eaten, today when left out, ratings: [{ dish: its name as planned, or dish_id, rating: good | okay | didnt_work, note?: what went well or didn't, in their words ("too oily"), said_by?: who said it }] }. One call for all of a reply. The latest rating and its note show the next time the dish is planned ("last time: too oily") on the Week page and in the cook's message; a short history is kept. A dish rated didnt_work is planned rarely, not never. Answers { dishes: [{ name, video, rating, note, rated_on, said_by, history }] }.

operations.name: get_dish
operations.description: What the app knows of one dish. { dish: its name as planned }. Answers { dish: { name, video: { url, title, thumbnail } or null, rating, note, rated_on, said_by, history: [{ rating, note, date, by }] } }, empty for a dish it knows nothing of.

agentInterface.instructions: Meal Planner owns this family's people, meals, the items they buy, their carts and recipes. Read the app before you answer and change it only through its operations, then tell the family what the app now says. A routine wake (the Sunday plan, the 15:00 and 19:00 reminders) names its own steps. What the app writes for the family (a plan's message and intro, a reminder's text, an order's message) is sent word for word. Nothing is ordered until the family replies or taps Order: "Order my <App> cart" is that yes. Call guide before a first conversation or when unsure which operation fits. Save the family's own words; never fill anything from guesses. A shared reel plus "save this" is a save_recipe call; for a dish it is also its video (set_dish_video). How a meal went is rate_dishes.
